clue.text: Cooperate to amalgamate drama and dance

parts.note: a drama is a play put on stage
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: An invitation to merge a theatre production with a dance show.
explanation.definitionFit: To play ball is an idiom for agreeing to work together with others.

clue.text: Bird breathin' with difficulty

definitions.meaning: a seabird with a striped beak found on northern cliffs
panting, written with the dropped final g as the clue's apostrophe shows

explanation.surface: A bird is described as gasping for air.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a black-and-white auk; 'puffin'' is the clipped spelling of puffing, meaning panting hard.

clue.text: Writer's hard on religious sect

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists; the 's stands for 'has'
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A novelist takes a tough line against a religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a Christian community in America known for shunning modern technology.

clue.text: Responsible for arguments backstage

definitions.meaning: read literally: being behind (responsible for) the scenes (rows, arguments)
out of public view, working away from the limelight

explanation.surface: Someone who starts rows yet stays hidden off-stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means secretly or out of public view, like theatre crew; read word by word it is causing scenes or rows.

clue.text: Look in outskirts of Leicester

indicators.note: only the edges of the town name are kept, its central letters being dropped

explanation.surface: A glance around the edge of a Midlands city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' keeps the first two and last two letters of LEICESTER, dropping ICEST from the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly or lecherous sidelong look.

clue.text: Secures employment in mine? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: the whole result of putting one word into the other is then read backwards
the word for employment goes inside the word for mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
use means employment of something

explanation.surface: Someone guarantees jobs at a colliery, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: USE inside PIT gives PUSEIT; 'Quite the reverse' then turns the whole thing round.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie up is to fasten or make something secure, and also to settle arrangements.

clue.text: Background notes

parts.note: looks like supporting research jottings, but means musical notes played behind a film or play

explanation.surface: Briefing papers giving context on a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Music composed to accompany a play or film plays in the background as atmosphere.

clue.text: Internal flight zone

parts.note: suggests a domestic air route, but the flight is a set of steps inside a building

explanation.surface: An area for domestic air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs runs up the vertical shaft inside a building that houses a staircase.

clue.text: Several shops together? One's in heaven

indicators.note: the letters for 'one is' go inside the word for a row of shops

parts.note: a parade is a row of shops along a street
one is: I (Roman numeral one) plus S for 'is'

explanation.surface: A shopping street makes someone feel blissfully happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is the abode of the blessed, a synonym for bliss in the afterlife.

clue.text: Having the blues in part of Eastern England is scary

indicators.note: the political word sits inside the name of the East Anglian region

parts.note: the Fens are low marshy lands in East Anglia
blue is the Conservative colour in Britain, so the blues are the political right

explanation.surface: Feeling depressed somewhere in East Anglia is a frightening experience.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics the Conservatives wear blue, so 'the blues' is the RIGHT, not sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that frightens alarms people, which is what being scary means.

clue.text: Shy female taking drug? What nonsense!

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
pish is an old exclamation of contempt

explanation.surface: A timid woman takes drugs and someone scoffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepish means bashful or embarrassed, a near synonym of timid.

clue.text: Church has cool alternative to pew

parts.note: to air a room is to cool and freshen it

explanation.surface: A church with a chilly atmosphere offers seating instead of benches.
explanation.definitionFit: A pew is a church bench; a single seat for one person is the other choice.

clue.text: Home help needed? It's being dealt with

parts.note: in means at home
a hand is help, as in lending a hand

explanation.surface: An advertisement asking for domestic assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter in hand is under control and being attended to.

clue.text: Offered to look after injured deer

parts.note: to tend is to care for

indicators.note: hurt, so the letters of the animal are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone volunteered to nurse a wounded deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendered means formally presented or put forward, as with a resignation.

clue.text: Alter nap arrangement during pregnancy?

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Changing sleep patterns while expecting a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Prenatal describes the time before birth, while a baby is being carried.

clue.text: Might they have featured in Reservoir Dogs?

definitions.text: Might they have featured in Reservoir Dogs?

parts.words: Might they have featured in Reservoir Dogs?
parts.note: the film title read literally: dogs that belong in a reservoir would be retrieving breeds at home in lakes

explanation.surface: A question about the cast of a Tarantino crime film.
explanation.definitionFit: These gundog breeds retrieve game from lakes and rivers, so they are dogs of the reservoir.

clue.text: Finished being absorbed

definitions.meaning: completed, as a meeting is concluded
engrossed, as in totally lost in something

explanation.surface: Someone done with work and deeply engrossed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means concluded and also preoccupied, as in being engrossed in one's work.

clue.text: With short piece of music, singer produces something remarkable

indicators.note: the word for a piece of music loses its last letter

parts.note: a score is a written musical composition
Cher is an American pop singer

explanation.surface: A vocalist with a brief tune turns out something outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorcher is informal British for something striking, such as a very hot day or a fierce shot.

clue.text: Go round and round collecting cases in a hotel

indicators.note: gathering the words together into a heap that is then rearranged

explanation.surface: A hotel porter going in circles gathering up suitcases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' is the anagram signal for CASESINAHOTEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase one's tail is an idiom for frantic activity that achieves nothing, like a dog circling.

clue.text: Cleric listened to drunken men

indicators.note: the clue's words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: wrecked is slang for very drunk; OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A priest hears some intoxicated men out.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is military shorthand for the other ranks, the soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a parish priest in the Church of England.

clue.text: Criticise a town for excessive greed

parts.note: to rap is to rebuke sharply
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a town for its avarice.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is grasping covetousness, the urge to seize more than one's share.

clue.text: Scientist hampered to a large extent

indicators.note: most of the next word is taken, its letters lying inside it

explanation.surface: A researcher was heavily obstructed in his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre-Marie Ampere was a French physicist who gave his name to the unit of electric current.

clue.text: Type of mushroom one cooked and served to most of family

indicators.note: prepared in the kitchen, so the letters are mixed up
the word for family loses its last letter

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A mushroom is fried and dished up to the relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns ONE into ENO; 'most of' cuts KIN to KI.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoki is a thin white Japanese mushroom with long stems.

clue.text: Student who often toils, primarily?

indicators.note: taking the leading letter of each word, the primary ones

explanation.surface: A description of a hard-working student.
explanation.definitionFit: A swot is British slang for a pupil who studies very hard.

clue.text: Oddly head teacher is duped

indicators.note: only the odd-numbered letters of the word are kept

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: Strangely, a headmaster has been tricked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' takes the 1st and 3rd letters of HEAD, giving HA.
explanation.definitionFit: To be had on is informal British for being fooled or teased.

clue.text: See old movie star on numerous occasions in English town

parts.note: lo means look or behold
Mae West, Hollywood star of the 1930s
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: Watch an old screen actress repeatedly in a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: Lowestoft is a coastal town in Suffolk, eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowestoft is a port on the Suffolk coast and Britain's most easterly town.

clue.text: Religious education and history courses

definitions.note: a meal made of several courses, so the plural stands for one noun

parts.note: RE is the school subject
the past is history

explanation.surface: A list of school subjects on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a meal, which is served as a series of dishes.

clue.text: Squatter, one given shelter by supermarket employee

indicators.note: the letter for one is housed inside the worker's title

parts.note: a stocker fills shelves in a shop
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A homeless squatter is taken in by a shop worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Squatter here is the comparative of squat, meaning shorter and broader.
